sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for Sininkere [sini1242] (refs: Diagne 2023 phonology; Kedrebeogo 1995 socling; ElCat 2022).
sources.note: Bibliography only; alternate names Silanke, Silinkere; AES 'shifting'.

sources.citation: Creissels, Denis. 2015. The inflectional role of tone in Soninke (West Mande). CALL 45 handout, Leiden. (and Creissels n.d. Flexion tonale en soninke) — held under soni1259
sources.note: Names Sillanka only as one of two outlier Soninke varieties ('Sillanka (an endangered Soninke variety spoken in Burkina-Faso)', p. 2) and analyses the Kingi variety (tonal, H/L with inflectional tone). No statement about Sillanka itself.

sources.citation: Kedrebeogo, Gerard. 1998. Language maintenance and language shift in Burkina Faso: The case of the Koromba. Studies in the Linguistic Sciences 28(2): 169-196 (Sillanko discussed pp. 172-192).
sources.note: Nothing: purely sociolinguistic (780 Sillanko of Bagkeemde village, Sanmatenga province, resisting shift to Moore/Fulfulde); no linguistic description of Sillanka at all.

sources.citation: Hantgan-Sonko, Abbie & Anna Marie Diagne. 2026. Isolate(d) Languages in the Sahel. Paper, Isolated Languages Workshop (HAL hal-05663884).

sources.note: The only linguistic description of Sillanka; Glottolog hhtype 'phonology'; abstract says it compares Sillanka phonology with Bakel and Kaedi Soninke, so it is the place a tone/accent statement would be. Brill landing page shows purchase options and an AWS-WAF CAPTCHA blocks automated access; Harvard has online access (HOLLIS docid cdi_crossref_primary_10_1163_19552629_01602009).

sources.note: Authoritative tonal description of Soninke proper (Kingi), the language of which Sillanka is an outlier dialect; cited by Diagne 2023 as the comparison baseline. Open on OpenEdition; relevant for soni1259 rather than sini1242, and would only support an inferred reading for Sillanka.
